The current wrangler config contains limits 200 actions/day and 20 rounds/run, but that does not prove an older deployed version has them.

Do not force Avi to debug those operator requirements through chat. Validate runtime settings at an appropriate startup/health/config boundary; expose a scoped readiness result to the browser with safe reasons and next actions. Reuse existing routes where possible. An unavailable workspace should display one concise setup state while retaining the user's draft/history. It must not invite an endless sequence of messages guaranteed to fail after queueing.

Use the existing verified handpicked registry and shared encrypted credential storage. Present full model display names. For Kerning dogfood, configure an actual usable default rather than leaving default_model NULL; use the existing guarded settings owner and evidence-backed choice. A model picker must use the same complete availability rules as the resolver (approval, lifecycle, required text/tools/stream capabilities, credential health). No automatic paid fallback or automatic enablement of secondary models.

Fix `/model default`: it may clear an override, but if no usable default exists, its recorded reply must say so and offer usable choices. It must not announce readiness. Do not conflate saving a key, verifying a key, and proving a live inference; keep those distinctions in operator evidence without putting jargon into ordinary conversation.

Add a minimal usable model/configuration control by reusing existing settings APIs. API keys remain a one-time masked/write-only field through the encrypted settings owner when needed. No dashboard, provider-management framework or required per-message command workflow.

First repair the existing queue route: use batch size 1 and a verified zero/lowest supported batch wait for interactive wake-ups, ensure the consumer is actually deployed, and prove ordinary input begins dispatch without invoking cron. A production binding alone is not evidence of a running consumer. Keep the queue as an execution trigger; queue hints must not replace D1 truth or authorize business writes.

A slice ending at a checkpoint must publish/schedule a near-term continuation. A contended wake must not disappear with all messages acknowledged while a later pending run waits until cron. Use the existing queue retry/send path to continue pending work, with a bounded delay for real contention rather than a busy loop. Inspect dispatch outcomes and durable pending work before acknowledging a consumed hint as finished. Continue to use existing leases/receipt/fence guards.

Use precise monotonic timestamps for accepted_at, dispatch_started_at, provider_started_at, first_public_text_at and finished_at in diagnostics. Acceptance response need not wait for generation. Local deterministic acceptance should wake an idle workspace immediately; dogfood target is dispatch beginning within one second in normal idle conditions, measured separately from provider response latency. Preserve existing payload caps and persist-before-publish guarantees. Do not create one D1 transaction per token. ## D1 economics containment — implemented 2026-10-04 (local only; deployed unverified)

Production exhausted the D1 free 100,000-writes/day budget with an idle app. The containment below is implemented and proven in this worktree only. Nothing here is deployed, and no historical production behavior is claimed fixed: the deployed worker may predate this source (notably the `touch: false` stream ticks), so deployed write sources must be re-measured after deploy, not inferred from this diff.

The `touch`/`touchIntervalSeconds` mechanism and its fire-and-forget `UPDATE sessions SET last_seen_at` are deleted (the column still records creation time; nothing reads `last_seen_at` — no cleanup, UI, or policy consumes it — so touches were eliminated, not re-debounced). Every GET scope route (`/api/me`, `/api/workspaces/:id`, all `requireWorkspaceScope` readers, SSE connect/reconnect/heartbeat polling) now costs zero D1 writes by construction. Remaining route-level writes are POST meaningful actions only (undo/command handlers in `routes/actions.ts`, message acceptance) — verified by grep, no GET-path writes remain.
### Executable evidence (all local workerd; deployed unverified)

- Rewritten `chat-api.integration.test.ts` touch test → `verifySession` never writes across repeated calls. Full worker project: 15 files / 238 tests green; web+pure: 27 files / 348 green (incl. R8 echo as deterministic acceptance-boundary proof — bubble with held network/nav, one identity — instead of wall-clock around `React.act`; the product 100ms target stands in design.md/docs, evidenced natively by `immediateEcho` in `plans/008-browser-evidence/synthetic-app-probe.json` / `two-send-probe.json`).

- Active 60s / 20-round answer (statements EXACT, rows ESTIMATE): accept ≈ 8 statements; previews up to 32 text batches/round = 640 batches × 3 statements (guard INSERT + chats UPDATE + run_activity INSERT) = 1,920 statements; thinking batches flush size-triggered (1,000 chars) or timer-triggered (400ms, 32-char floor), so the 24k char cap does NOT imply ≤24 rows — worst case approaches 24,000/32 ≈ 750 tiny rows per run; end receipts ≈ 2/round. Rows written depends on index accounting — present structures are row + PK plus `(chat_id, cursor)` on `run_activity`; NO universal multiplier is assumed here. Indicatively, at ~2 rows_written per statement a heavy answer costs low-thousands rows (previews alone), but the real factor must come from D1 metadata after deploy, not this doc. Per-round caps do not bound the run (whole-run discipline proposed in 014 as zero preview rows, not a persisted cap).

- Transient display (ephemeral-eligible, see 014): `text_chunk` (≤640/run by the per-round cap), thinking batches (flush-timing dependent, worst case ~750/run), heartbeats (already network-only). Business facts (must stay durable): `message_accepted`, `answer_saved`, `action_applied`/`action_reverted`, receipts, checkpoints, completion rows.

- Residual risks (not fixed here): idle reads approach half the free tier at 10 tabs (push fanout in 014 addresses it); long-run preview writes are unbounded per run (zero preview rows proposed in 014); the incident's exact deployed write mix is unmeasured — redeploy + D1 dashboard required, not assumed. Hibernation gives no universal zero-cost, sub-10ms, or disconnect-resilience guarantee.

Register `/model`, `/workspace`, `/today`, `/undo` and `/help` through Telegram's native bot command menu, with `/sheet` added only after plan 012 works and `/start` reserved for linking. Generate names/descriptions from plan 007's shared registry; refresh Telegram's advertised list when a feature becomes available. The bot also accepts typed commands, including Telegram's `/name@<this bot>` form, through the same parser/dispatcher and authorization as web. `/model` without an argument shows the current chat model and available handpicked keys; `/model <key>` changes only the sender's current Otis chat; `/model default` clears its override. Callback model choices carry an opaque server-side ID and revalidate membership/availability; typed form remains available. Commands are optional shortcuts: `/today` reads saved brief/current due work without creating another scheduled brief; `/sheet` is an authenticated download after plan 012; `/undo` follows shared contracts, defaulting to the selected successful action and later successful writes in that same run, with “Undo only this action” as the alternative. A dependency conflict asks before commit. `/help` explains natural-language examples. Every command/callback can be expressed as ordinary conversation. Inline Undo/Done/Draft actions use opaque server IDs, verify current identity/workspace/action scope/replay status, and answerCallbackQuery promptly. Snooze/Change ask for a date or value instead of choosing tomorrow. Each successful write explains what changed and exposes Undo. Escape user content for Telegram HTML. Long work gets a truthful concise status. Unsupported photo/location retains metadata only; do not download or claim it was processed.

2. Implement text receive/send and connect Telegram's native command menu and typed commands to the shared inbox/command dispatcher from plan 007. Verify a command chosen from Telegram's menu or typed manually yields the same authorized result as web, with no provider call; `/start` remains linking-only. Verify `/model` lists only credentialed approved choices, changes only the sender's active Otis chat, and does not alter another member's chat or a running turn. Duplicate webhook delivery must create one accepted input, one run and one set of ledger effects. Outbound `sendMessage` may have an unknown outcome after a lost response; represent that state and do not claim exactly-once delivery or blindly resend. A linked account's action is attributed to the right Otis user. Use mocked Telegram HTTP calls in CI.

3. Implement callback registration, validation and actions. Verify callback replay cannot double-undo/complete a task; wrong member/workspace is denied; missing date enters clarification; callbacks are acknowledged while long work is queued.

## Current-code hazards to repair as part of planned tests

claims.text: Codex reviewer, 2026-10-04. These are corrections inside the assigned task, not a new gate or acceptance verdict. Current helper read on this date; source may change while implementation continues. Read exact current source before fixing. No reviewer subagents.

1. `resolveTelegramTarget` looks up the first telegram_users row by user_id and takes destination from the original source. Probe source sender/chat 777 plus first own binding 888 returns telegramUserId888/chat777. Resolve exact source sender, private chat, original source user/workspace and matching current identity binding. Otherwise a removed original binding can still receive data because a different surviving own binding passes the delivery check. Never substitute another identity by arbitrary first row. Validate destination against the original normalized source, not only a mutable outbox payload; source channel must be Telegram. Legacy multiple bindings must not retarget.

3. `deliverTelegramOutbox` currently captures now once for the whole loop. A 10-second send or paced multipart work makes later claims/retry_after stale. Use fresh operation timestamps (inject a clock for deterministic tests if needed). Compute retry deadline from the actual response time, not invocation start. Persist actual claim/send-result times. A stale-sending timeout must not classify a newly started later send as old because the loop reused an earlier clock.

4. Claim UPDATE checks only pending, while due/max-attempt checks were read earlier. Include current retry eligibility and attempt bound in claim. A paused reader must not claim a row that another sender has returned to pending with a future retry_after. Use actual claimed attempt count, not a stale SELECT value. The guided-linking addition remains authoritative; link route currently read before those new instructions was only a basic issuer, so its missing status/workspace intent is not yet a completion finding. Current helper inspected while implementation is running; these are verified scoped corrections, not acceptance.

4. **Link UI expiry and stale async actions** (`TelegramConnection.tsx`). Automatic status checks stop after two minutes, and expiry is checked only after a later status response, so a ten-minute-old link stays Open Telegram forever without interaction. Use a bounded local expiry timeout independent of status reads. Connect/disconnect async completions need workspace-generation/unmount checks, as the initial GET already has: a pending workspace-A issuer response must never install A's link into workspace-B settings. 1. **Immediate continuation is missing at entrypoints.** Current index.ts queue telegram_delivery branch runs deliverTelegramOutbox once then continues; normal dispatch likewise once. No delaySeconds/next-delivery wake scheduling exists in index.ts or dispatchHint.ts. Selection excludes later multipart parts until predecessor delivered, so a long reply commonly sends only part zero and leaves later parts until five-minute cron. Rate-limited rows likewise get a correct next_retry_at but no wake at that deadline. Extend existing bounded delivery summary/helper to expose whether eligible continuation exists and its earliest safe delay; publish a delayed hint on the EXISTING queue after delivery at production entrypoints. Respect per-chat pacing/retry_after; schedule no hints for only unknown/failed/blocked parts. Handle remaining work after batch limit too. No new queue or persistent polling. 1. **Agent checkpoint continuation missing.** index.ts queue normal dispatch awaits dispatchWorkspace(budget3) and delivery, ignores dispatch results. dispatchWorkspace stops immediately when detail=checkpoint/deferred. No subsequent agent wake is published. Long turns with more than the per-slice rounds therefore still need cron even though Telegram multipart delivery now has its own continuation. Use existing results + a bounded pending-work check to schedule the existing workspace hint for successful checkpoint/budget remainder. Genuine contention/lost lease must not spin immediate hints: delayed/backstop under existing bounded policy. No new scheduler. Add entrypoint regression with a handler/provider that needs a second slice: queue invocation schedules next workspace wake; processing that wake finishes without scheduled(). Also prove waiting_for_input creates no continuation and contended lease does not immediate-loop.

2. **Telegram undo missing source + split commit.** executeTelegramCommand explicitly passes sourceMessageId:undefined to runTelegramUndo before the messages_in INSERT batch. Undo's ledger receipt/events therefore have no inbound source, and its effects/run/reply commit before the source/command-delivery operation. A failure of the latter can leave a business undo with no accepted command/delivery. The 009A command integration test exercises /model default + unknown only; it does not prove /undo, /thinking, /today or /workspace. Compose the existing ledger extra-statements boundary with source receipt/command result/delivery for successful undo, preserving stable action ID and author/latest/from_here rules. Do not invent a parallel undo engine. Add a real Telegram /undo of a previous real ledger change, assert source provenance and delivery; inject failure at the true committing tail and assert no partial undo/source/reply; retry/redelivery must change no extra event/revision. Cover specified remaining command effects with actual persisted assertions and no provider calls.

Keep 009A review pending. The successful tests and earlier corrected helpers are real progress; these two local correctness/user-flow gaps are the remaining review findings identified so far, not a request for broader architecture work.

**In-transaction redemption authority is incomplete.** telegram.ts start-code precheck correctly rejects a Telegram binding owned by another user and verifies requested_workspace_id membership. But the committing `link_redemptions.guard_ok` subquery checks only link_codes.id/unconsumed/expiry; the following ON CONFLICT telegram_users statement unconditionally replaces user_id. If another account links the Telegram ID, or requested membership is removed, after the precheck but before this batch, the stale redemption can take over that binding or consume/link to a revoked workspace. Put existing conflict-ownership predicate plus requested-workspace current membership into the same guard. On verified guard failure return truthful conflict/unavailable without code consumption; on actual storage failure keep retryable error. Test paused/precheck-to-batch conflicting binding and revoked intent, asserting unchanged existing identity, unconsumed code, no success confirmation. headings: # 009A — reviewer-authored Telegram text capture, reply and retrieval
## 6. Deliver, retry and recover without another engine
## 8. Decisive tests, not a mock conversation disconnected from production
## 10. Current official references checked by reviewer

claims.text: A linked Avi or Hunor sends a text to the private bot, Otis starts processing from an immediate wake hint and replies in that private chat. Explicit facts are recorded once through the existing ledger. A later text retrieves those facts through the same existing agent/query tools. A missing detail asks one question; Telegram's native Reply targets that question and resumes its saved operation. Commands change real scoped settings rather than going to the model.

Clear complete instructions save directly. Save a clear fact while a separate missing task date is awaiting clarification. Do not infer warm/cold status or invent a deadline/time. Existing explicit no-deadline behavior remains supported. Text-only acceptance is not full 009 or voice acceptance.

- `apps/worker/src/inbox/telegram.ts`: /start redemption, routing, author chat, text acceptance and workspace_actor outbox. Raw link code is already redacted. Dedupe returns stored inbox status cast to a smaller result union, lacks stable run ID on replay; inspect and correct narrowly. Other slash commands currently become ordinary agent text. No targeted answer branch.
- `apps/worker/src/dispatchHint.ts`: existing best-effort queue hint after durable acceptance. Reuse it; no cron as normal wake mechanism.

- `apps/worker/src/actor/dispatch.ts`: completeRun writes final reply plus activity; waitForInput writes/retains pending question and releases slot; failRunTerminal records failure. None enqueues Telegram sends. Existing dispatch scans only destination workspace_actor. Existing recovery must continue ignoring Telegram sends.

- `apps/worker/src/routes/commands.ts`: executeCommand is the shared deterministic interpreter and returns effects. Its HTTP acceptance/Undo adapters are web-specific; do not fake a web session/cookie to invoke them.

- `apps/worker/src/inbox/repository.ts`: reference for current authorized acceptance, command effects and model/thinking pinning. Reuse small helpers if needed; do not replace the web acceptance path wholesale.

Webhook route with missing required bot token must be disabled truthfully before acknowledging new conversational work; pure inbox tests may still test acceptance without transport config. Test fixtures use a clearly synthetic token and fake HTTP, never a real endpoint/key. Do not depend on globally disabling fetch in a way that hides real production wiring.

Implement `POST /api/workspaces/:workspaceId/telegram/link` using requireWorkspaceScope with csrf, current session and membership. Generate 24 random bytes as 32 unpadded base64url characters; store only SHA-256 hash bound to the trusted user, ten-minute UTC expiry and unconsumed state in existing link_codes. Return the one-time deep link `https://t.me/<configured username>?start=<code>` plus expiry; Cache-Control no-store. GET/session reads must not mint codes or write last_seen. Do not accept caller user ID. Existing consume remains atomic and hash-only. Membership changed between issuing and consuming is rechecked by routing; linking does not grant workspace access.

Private /start confirmation may be a concise administrative response after successful redemption. Unlinked or ambiguous users get generic linking/workspace guidance, no business data. Where no workspace is resolved, the existing outbox cannot represent workspace-less sends: allow one best-effort, bounded administrative reply after persisting the unrouted/start result. No automatic retry, no model invocation, no new global outbox framework. Document this exception; duplicate updates must not repeatedly send it. Never echo the link code. Unknown administrative delivery is not claimed successful.
## 4. Inbound acceptance and commands

Ordinary text: resolve linked identity, current memberships and active author chat; one membership may auto-select, several without valid choice must ask. Persist one source/member chat message/run/activity/dispatch intent atomically. Pin effective model key and thinking request as the web acceptance does; a subsequent /model or /thinking must not change an already accepted run. No model call during acceptance. Publish the queue hint only after the commit, including matching replay when a lost earlier hint might need repair. Hint failure never rolls back accepted input.

Apply model/thinking effects plus command receipt/reply atomically with source acceptance and current membership/author checks. /workspace changes only this Telegram identity's selection, clears stale chat mapping and validates target membership inside the batch. Web selection and teammate chat/model remain unchanged. Before a selected workspace exists, /workspace may list the trusted user's memberships or choose an exact unambiguous one; never require a model or silently select the first.

Undo delegates to existing ledger target/dependency/revision rules with the Telegram source as provenance and a stable action ID derived from inbound ID. Do not call web routes with synthetic authentication or disable confirmation/dependency checks. Factor the shared domain operation if necessary, not a framework. Default targets the author's latest reversible action in this Otis chat and uses existing from_here semantics; repeated delivery replays its receipt. If a dependency is disputed, ask narrowly rather than rewriting teammate history. Commands need no model or active mutation lease, but their committing boundary must still guard membership and affected state.

Persist command answer/delivery as part of that guarded operation. Optional native bot command registration is not a gate blocker and must not call Telegram from CI; leave it for an explicit operator command if not already provisioned. Never advertise a feature as available merely because it is listed in the registry.

Use deterministic delivery IDs: source/input ID + response kind/key + part index, with a stored payload version. Final uses run ID; question uses clarification ID (two questions in one run must get distinct keys); command/admin source uses inbox ID. Do not use a newly random ID for every redispatch. INSERT OR IGNORE is acceptable only for this immutable identical delivery key, not for swallowing conflicting source context. Typed payload includes trusted user/workspace/Otis chat, bot installation, private destination ID, run/source IDs, logical kind, text/part index, previous-part ID, and optional clarification ID. No credentials or private thinking payloads.

Resolve the actual pending question ID even when the ledger already persisted it and waitForInput's alreadyPending branch skips insertion. Retain one canonical clarification. Enqueue its question once in the same parking transition. A resumed question must not be resent on successful completion. Final reply text is the same content as saved chat_messages; failure text is concise and says input is retained and, when relevant, which actions actually committed. Never present internal stack traces or token paths.

Add one bounded deliverTelegramOutbox helper, called after dispatch slices and from explicit Telegram delivery hints. Queue/cron must also discover pending Telegram deliveries when the run is already terminal; existing listWorkspacesNeedingRecovery only finds actor intents/nonterminal runs and is insufficient by itself. Add a small bounded Telegram-due scan, not a rewrite of recovery. Existing recoverWorkspace must not reset Telegram sending to pending.

Use one bounded POST sendMessage with JSON, AbortController timeout 10 seconds and no credentials beyond the configured server token. A missing token is known preflight failure, not an ambiguous attempted send. Response body success must be valid, ok true, and contain a matching private chat/message ID. Persist returned bot message ID in that delivery payload for clarification routing. Success update is claim-owner scoped, never overwrites another owner/status. No transaction spans provider/Telegram I/O.

- Network exception/timeout, 5xx without a trustworthy rejection, malformed/truncated response, process crash while sending, or success response followed by inability to record success -> outcome_unknown, never automatically pending. Telegram sendMessage has no implemented idempotency key here. Do not claim exactly-once outward delivery.

Bound delivery work to five eligible items per invocation, one private-chat send per second. Long multi-part responses progress by part dependency and delayed hint; no high-frequency D1 scheduler or polling loop. Queue body gets explicit kind telegram_delivery, workspace_id; branches must not feed delivery rows to agent dispatch. Failure to publish a hint leaves the durable row discoverable. Use no new queue/infrastructure unless a demonstrated existing binding limitation is reported first.

Dispatch continuation checkpoints must also publish another immediate hint when work remains rather than relying on cron after budget is exhausted. Avoid endless redispatch of genuine lease contention: delayed retry/backstop, bounded message attempts. Best-effort typing is optional and can be omitted from this checkpoint; no permanent timer, per-token HTTP or D1 writes merely to show typing.

Persist the answer in messages_in and the same author chat with run_id belonging to the waiting run. Do not create a second agent run or mutate business state in acceptance. Store target clarification ID with the source/fingerprint for replay, then use existing resumeRun with explicit clarificationId, persisted messageId and server-derived author. A crash between acceptance and resume must be repaired by replay/recovery using that durable target, not lost or guessed. If resume rejects a date/detail, retain the pending question and answer source and send a concise request for the needed detail; do not mark it resolved. Exactly targeted replay of an already-used answer cannot resolve the next question.

Unsupported media with text retains its existing explicit confirmation policy. Metadata-only unsupported input may get a concise response; no download/transcription. Voice must state it is not supported yet instead of entering a text model as opaque media.

New real workerd/D1 integration suite, migrations through current last file, synthetic users/workspaces, fake Telegram HTTP. Test actual webhook acceptance and actual delivery entrypoint wiring. Also run a scripted fake ProviderAdapter through the real AgentHandler for tool orchestration: do not prove business memory by an EchoHandler that simply repeats input.

Required journey: linked Hunor sends an explicit synthetic Bistro fact -> immediate hint is observed -> queue/dispatch handler executes a real ledger write -> real completion batch creates delivery -> fake sendMessage sees the saved answer -> later query retrieves the stored value -> no extra events on webhook/queue replay. Keep fake model output tied to expected calls and actual tool result; assertions inspect D1 and outbound text, not just call counts. Echo is acceptable only for isolated entrypoint wiring tests.
2. Duplicate and simultaneous webhook acceptance creates one run/source/effect/delivery; no cron needed for ordinary wake. Storage failure returns retryable non-200, not accepted fiction.

5. Question parking releases the slot; another member completes; native reply resumes exact typed pending task once; invalid date/old question/foreign requester/replay retain correct state. Crash after answer acceptance repairs on duplicate/recovery.
8. Bot token missing disables conversational webhook; transport mocks cannot contact real Telegram. Exceptions/logging cannot include token or link code.

Stop and report a narrow blocker if current shared command or clarification API cannot provide required authorization/idempotency without broad surgery, if outgoing work cannot be atomically tied to the saved result, or if ordinary operation exceeds the real Worker/D1 invocation limits. Do not paper over it with a cron wait, a fabricated answer, insecure user IDs or another service. Reviewer decides scope changes; implementation agent does not rewrite this plan.

headings: # Gate 010 handoff: automatic native audio and Groq transcription

claims.text: Decision recorded 2026-10-01. Execution supplement to [010-voice.md](010-voice.md). Keep the original dependency order; do not start a separate voice project ahead of foundations. Current source and migration state must be inspected when 010 begins.

Members record/send a voice note without choosing speech infrastructure. Otis selects a verified native transcription route when the conversation model supports the actual format; otherwise it uses configured Groq STT and gives the selected model the transcript. Native audio capability is not required for text/tool-model approval. The selected conversation model remains unchanged.
| Native unsupported/unverified for format, and Groq candidate/configuration/credential verified | `groq_stt` |

Do not probe support on every recording, infer it from model names, or send bytes to multiple services to discover a winner. Native authentication, quota and outage errors are not unsupported capability. They produce their own error; do not reroute silently. If another route is desired, ask conversationally or let the member explicitly change configuration. Groq fallback from a known unsupported/unverified native route is already authorized by workspace setup; do not ask per message.

Snapshot conversation model, route and registry version at acceptance; confirm against server-validated actual format before inference. If metadata invalidates the preliminary route, finalize an authorized compatible route before sending anything, or fail clearly. `/model` affects future turns, not a pending recording. Report effective voice support through configured STT separately from native support.

Extend the existing provider credential allowlist/types/validation to support `groq` as an STT-only provider. Inspect every exhaustive switch, contract serializer, metadata route and fixture before changing the enum. Preserve AES-GCM workspace/provider/version AAD and member rechecks. Do not create a parallel raw-key table or a browser VITE key. Conversation adapters must not treat every credential provider as a chat provider.

Verify current key against fixed Groq endpoints using an authorized bounded synthetic test. Authentication/discovery alone does not verify transcript quality. Credential replacement resets verification and stale verification of key A cannot mark key B valid; reuse the provider-gate race protection. Membership must still exist when configuration commits.

Official documentation lists WebM, MP4/M4A and OGG upload support; actual device/container/codec tests are still required. Enforce the lower verified byte limit, not the playground's displayed limit alone. Avoid transcoding until an actual supported-format failure proves a need. Test silence, corrupted bytes and empty transcript. Transcription output is member-attributed derived text; it is not permission to bypass existing clarification/tool policies.

6. Atomically mark ready and create/release the existing agent dispatch intent. Agent retries/reconnects reuse the committed transcript. Recovery can reconstruct missing dispatch intent from durable state. Do not create a second logical agent run for a retry.

Idempotency is local logical exactly-once, not guaranteed provider inference exactly-once. A lost response after Groq accepted a request may require another bounded transcription request. An already committed transcript must not be retranscribed. Use stable source/media/route identity; per-attempt random IDs do not replace the logical receipt key. Tests must distinguish external requests from canonical transcript/agent effects.
## Tests and acceptance
| Test | Required result |
| Unsupported or unverified native format | Configured verified Groq selected; conversation model unchanged |
| Missing STT configuration/key | Voice unavailable; no unauthorized provider request |

Run root typecheck/lint/test/build and diff checks, plus Plan 010 native-browser/device review. Do not use Playwright. Leave source reviewable; report implemented schema/routes/contracts, effective voice availability, Groq model choice and evidence, deterministic test counts, actual device/provider evidence or specific blockers, quotas/errors and remaining limitations. - Acceptance: unsent text/voice in two workspaces, then open a deleted chat in one; unrelated authorized entries remain recoverable and never reroute. Actual removed membership purges only that workspace; expired/replaced account cannot send stale content.

- User impact: a transient network failure is described as missing evidence; Refresh preview can leave the saved change stuck in Loading with no detail. Inspection is essential for trustworthy correction/undo.

- Smallest fix: explicit loading/network-error/not-retained states, Retry for the actual failed read, clear stale error/detail when selecting a different resource, and refresh action plus preview when required. Reuse existing scoped API functions.

- Acceptance: fail each read once, click its recovery action, receive the same scoped resource without mutation; expired/forgotten source remains honestly unavailable; access loss still closes content.

- Priority: P1 for reliable retrieval. Confidence HIGH on missing read capability; actual model-answer failure rate unmeasured. Effort M. Fix risk LOW/MED: add a bounded scoped read, not a second memory store.

- User impact: after saving a phone, price or other business field, later retrieval must infer current truth from notes or page through raw events. Corrections/disputes/undo require deterministic projection reads; asking the model to reconstruct the ledger is unreliable.

- Acceptance: save field → separate chat retrieval → correction → retrieval → undo → retrieval, all with canonical values/source links; disputed fields never become confident answers; other-workspace and removed-member access denied.

- Evidence: `packages/agent/src/tools.ts:158–159` allows `snooze_until?: string | null`, but its validator (`:610`) converts null to undefined, causing recipient-style missing-patch rejection for an unsnooze-only request. The provider declaration (`:1242`) advertises only string. `packages/ledger/src/reducers/tasks.ts:48–50` already supports explicit null to clear the snooze. Update due similarly needs schema support for an explicit no-deadline value.
- Acceptance: snooze → unsnooze-only tool request produces one event and reappears in due work; omission preserves snooze, invalid instant is rejected, due/title unchanged.
- Priority: P1. Confidence HIGH on the missing boundary; production reproduction not attempted. Effort M. Fix risk MED: cross-tab identity must fail closed without deleting unrelated work.

- Smallest fix: existing API acceptance boundary verifies the caller's expected session/account against the authenticated session as a rejection precondition; cross-tab logout/account-change notification and foreground revalidation promptly detach old UI/flush owners. Client IDs remain non-authoritative: a match never grants access.

- Acceptance: two local authenticated sessions sharing a workspace, held A new-chat outbox, cookie replaced by B, then flush; no A content is accepted or shown as B, same-account reconnect still works, existing-chat author denial remains intact.

- Acceptance: instrument a quiet chat and an active chat with many prior runs; routine connection rotation does not issue full snapshots, real missing cursor does, removed membership closes content, no DB poll per token.
### SOL-18 — Missing member timezone is silently represented as UTC

- Smallest fix: represent unknown timezone honestly and ask only when local/relative date resolution needs it; persist an explicitly confirmed member timezone through the existing preference path. If suggesting the browser zone, treat it as a suggestion to confirm. Setting a date timezone must not enable a brief or invent its schedule/channel.

- Acceptance: new member with no timezone, relative deadline, explicit absolute instant, and two members in different zones; ambiguous local times ask, explicit instants remain usable, no implicit brief schedule appears.

- Acceptance: leap/nonleap February, invalid month/day/zone, offset-free instant, DST gap/overlap, valid date and valid offset-bearing instant through the actual tool/ledger path; rejected values create no event.

- Acceptance: ordinary member-created task belongs to that member, deliberate team/unassigned task remains unassigned, valid teammate assignment works, removed/cross-workspace assignees fail, brief selection reflects the saved owner.

- Acceptance: add → verify → remove → use platform fallback; repeat deletion safely; no platform key produces an honest unavailable state; another workspace/member without credential-management authority cannot remove it; concurrent replacement is guarded.

- Smallest fix: measure seeded realistic workspace sizes under actual local Workers/D1, then bound indexed candidate retrieval and load only command-required projections while retaining the existing atomic preconditions/receipts. Reuse the existing runtime cost checkpoint; no ORM, vector DB, cache-as-authority or distributed coordination redesign.

- Acceptance: record rows read/written, CPU and request counts for common capture/read/correction/undo flows at expected workspace sizes; fail the gate on unbounded growth; retain ambiguity detection, deterministic replay and late-batch rollback coverage.

- User impact: a business conversation from last month can be present and accessible while Search says there is no match. A user must repeatedly load older pages before their query works, making retained memory difficult to find.

- Acceptance: matching chat beyond the first page is found, genuinely absent title shows no match only after the scoped search finishes, access-revoked/team boundaries remain enforced, request count remains bounded.

- Acceptance: changing reply preference leaves English UI metadata correct, response preference persists, multilingual response metadata follows the actual content where available, screen-reader spot check recorded.

- Acceptance: question, conditional, reported quote, mixed entities and direct commands through the actual tool boundary; ambiguous/inferred cases ask without mutation; explicit scoped commands apply once.

- Acceptance: both dev entrypoints and actual Storybook stories render; short exchange compared at all five mandated widths; production styles/Inter load; checker and actual browser evidence recorded independently.

- Acceptance: actual Workers/DO separation with subscriber and executor in distinct contexts, restart/reconnect and two clients; every persisted public event reaches authorized listeners in order, no duplicate effects or per-token database polling. Tests must exercise the production branch, not only `pollIntervalMs` injection.

- Acceptance: open the actual default production branch, remove member/revoke session, then publish new activity; removed subscriber receives no post-revocation private event and closes with the correct signal. Retained members continue, scope is checked on reconnect, row-read budget is recorded.

- Smallest fix: publish the actual committed authorized row/ID/cursor from the existing activity owner; idempotent replay must preserve that identity and avoid duplicate publication effects. Keep append-before-publish/fence checks, stable ordering and current authority. Do not synthesize a cursor or bypass the existing durable owner.

- Acceptance: initial snapshot cursor > 0, new default-path publication reaches the browser with the next persisted cursor and SSE ID, duplicate key/restart does not add another event, lost response catches up without duplicate text, stale executor cannot publish new public content.
- Priority/effort/risk/confidence: P1 for brief acceptance; M/L; MED; HIGH source evidence. Owning plan 011.

- Acceptance: actual scheduled entrypoint tick at two members' chosen times yields one canonical brief each; duplicate tick/restart yields no duplicate; disabled/empty schedules remain silent; “second one” targets the original saved task after other work changes.
- User impact: “Remind me tomorrow at 10” can become a task but cannot substantiate a promise to notify at 10. A closed web app has no implemented push delivery.
- Priority/effort/risk/confidence: P2 after chosen briefs; M/L; MED; HIGH missing capability. Owning plan 011.

- Lean completion: use the existing job/outbox/scheduling infrastructure for a deliberately chosen one-off time/zone/channel. Until implemented, keep replies truthful about saved task versus actual notification; no proactive nudge engine, default morning time or paid service.
- Acceptance: one explicit reminder fires once, across restart/repeated cron and DST cases, with clear in-app-only versus connected Telegram behavior; no promised closed-browser push.
- Priority/effort/risk/confidence: draft handoff P2; export P3 after useful capture/retrieval; M then L; MED; HIGH missing capability. Owning plan 012.

- Acceptance: missing phone still permits copy; revised draft preserves recipient; URL-encoded handoff stays draft; explicit confirmation records once; future workbook uses one snapshot and membership-checked expiry.

- Lean completion: owner-defined server recovery using saved logical steps/receipts and current state, with an attached Continue/Retry control only when that boundary is implemented. Show partial writes and their undo controls; do not re-post the original instruction as automatic recovery.

- Acceptance: provider fails before writes and after one committed write; controlled recovery completes once without repeating that write, handles changed facts/membership, and distinguishes Stop from Undo.

`pnpm exec vitest run --config plans/qa/sol-audit-2026-10-05.config.ts`: **16/16 defect reproductions passed**, 1 file, 947 ms on the latest run. These intentionally assert existing incorrect behavior; green is evidence of defects, NOT acceptance of the product. Covers SOL-01, SOL-02 (negation/question/quotation), SOL-03 (recipient-only exception/content-only data loss), SOL-04 (combined status/title patch), SOL-15 (null unsnooze), SOL-19 (invalid/underspecified deadlines), SOL-20 (omitted assignee), SOL-25 (status questions/conditionals/quotes), and SOL-29 (zero-cursor collision).
- `pnpm check:stories`: passed, 92 required fixture IDs across 16 story files. This does not establish that Storybook renders.

Short text wraps within captured views; desktop has scoped sidebar/chat and source/action inspection uses the existing surfaces. Current composition visibly adds a model selector row inside the composer and substantial gaps around Working. The former conflicts with the currently approved no-toolbar recipe; structural resolution belongs to the other agent's already-assigned reference/model work. Checker green does not resolve that contract mismatch. No full visual acceptance claimed.

1. **Block incorrect or unauthorized work:** SOL-27/28/29 in the existing realtime assignment; SOL-02/25 intent; SOL-10 disputed drafts; SOL-06/12/16 account/scope cleanup and acceptance. Handle transport regression within its current owner rather than starting a competing stream implementation.
2. **Make capture/recovery reliable:** SOL-01/05/11. Keep submitted payloads and UUIDs immutable, preserve unknown acceptance, and make visible Retry actually retry the failed operation.

6. **Prove affordability and fidelity:** SOL-17 revalidated against concurrent source, SOL-22 actual runtime measurements, SOL-24 language semantics and SOL-26 working review wrappers. Run the owning application's required checks when implementing; no gate is completed by this report.
| Journey / controls | Inspected evidence | Outstanding acceptance |
| Briefs, explicit reminders, outward draft handoff, exports | Source/migrations/contracts and owning plans cross-checked | GAP-A/B/C/D remain implementation work, not feature acceptance |

Considered and not promoted into extra work: no CRM/dashboard, speculative vector search, new notification engine or second queue; projection reducers' shallow map copies alone are not a proved persistence defect because the executor snapshots fingerprints before handlers; existing multi-field bulk confirmation is enforced by the handler and should not be reported missing merely because the pure round collector does not call it. Keep these checks tied to real paths rather than adding speculative refactors.

claims.text: Status: expanded audit complete through observation 63, including read-only Wrangler production metadata/insights/query plans, real local D1 budgets, background scheduling, startup, voice, API/session handling, settings UX and native-harness/model integration research. Prioritized recommendations and reproducible evidence follow. The linked model audit records one deployed acceptance-to-completion sample; matched end-to-end phase latency remains unmeasured. Continue this log when implementing or profiling deployed traffic.

- Discovery 4: ordinary acceptance chooses the Queue before the already-bound workspace actor (`apps/worker/src/dispatchHint.ts:18-45`). Wrangler specifies batch size 10 and no batch timeout. Queue startup latency and whether its consumer runs in the same place as SSE need immediate verification; direct actor wake-up already exists as fallback.

- Discovery 6: repeated membership/model/credential reads exist across acceptance, dispatch, handler setup, model selection and each provider round (`apps/worker/src/inbox/repository.ts:524`, `apps/worker/src/actor/dispatch.ts:957-962`, `apps/worker/src/agent/handler.ts:143-164`, `apps/worker/src/providers/service.ts:153-181,234-242`). Consolidate within each trusted execution boundary; keep authoritative membership checks at acceptance and mutation boundaries.

- Discovery 15: after every successful send the client invalidates the entire chat snapshot (`apps/web/src/ConversationScreen.tsx:440`). A snapshot performs four parallel HTTP reads followed by a request for every run in the loaded transcript (`apps/web/src/api/snapshot.ts:34-48`). Long chats therefore incur an HTTP N+1 and re-download old activity on every send/resync. Patch the acceptance into the existing cache and refresh only the new run; load historical run details on inspection.

- Vetting correction to Discovery 11: the registry's `defaultChoiceId: 'medium'` is **not applied by message acceptance**. With no explicit chat effort, `resolveThinkingSnapshot` persists `{kind:'provider_default'}` (`apps/worker/src/inbox/repository.ts:249-268`), and the adapter omits `thinking_level`. Do not present medium effort as the cause of this user's Flash-Lite latency. Google's documented native default is already minimal.

- Discovery 19: the stable system prompt hardcodes Kerning (`packages/agent/src/prompt.ts:17`) although the dynamic context already provides workspace name (`:59`). This can make another workspace receive wrong-business answers. Replace that one baked-in name with workspace-neutral wording; no architecture change required.

- Architecture follow-up requested by user: consult current Cloudflare documentation and compare Workflows, Queues, Durable Objects, D1 placement/batching and real-time transport. Recommendations must explain what existing work each service removes, its latency/cost tradeoff, and why adopting it would be simpler than the current implementation.

- Discovery 20: persisted lifecycle events are not consistently broadcast at all. `completeRun` appends a full-answer `text_chunk` and `run_finished` to its D1 batch (`apps/worker/src/actor/dispatch.ts:507-523`), but the actor dispatch module has no `liveChatBus` publication. Acceptance and ledger action events similarly have durable-only publishers. Even after moving generation into the actor, explicitly publish **committed** lifecycle events there; otherwise completion/UI reconciliation still relies on catch-up and refresh timers.

- Cloudflare architecture evidence (2026-10-06): [Workflows](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/get-started/guide/) provides durable steps, retries and waits, but [Free pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/reference/pricing/) includes only 3,000 steps/day and 10 ms CPU/invocation. It is a potential simplification for long-lived background jobs, not evidence that a chat token will arrive sooner. [Durable Object pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/pricing/) bills active wall-clock duration; persistent SSE/timers prevent idle hibernation. Hibernating [WebSockets](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/best-practices/websockets/) are a separate optional cost improvement, not required to fix the current route.

- Discovery 30: switching the immediate wake-up to `ctx.waitUntil(stub.fetch(...))` alone must account for the [Worker's 30-second post-response lifetime](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/best-practices/workers-best-practices/), while provider rounds allow 60 seconds. The actor must own continued execution/liveness and durable recovery; do not fire-and-forget work in an ordinary Worker or drop the only awaited actor request. Keep Queue/cron as backstops and verify disconnect/long-turn behavior.

- Architecture consideration: [D1 locality](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/configuration/data-location/) and [DO locality](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/reference/data-location/) can amplify each serial read. Current remote regions and placement are unverified; adding a hint does not move an existing object/database. Inspect query `meta` timing/served region and deployment metrics before proposing placement changes. Edge placement alone does not make a single writable D1 database local everywhere.

- Voice scope observation (in-progress working tree): acceptance can select native audio (`apps/worker/src/inbox/repository.ts:567-580,771-772`), but the Worker transcription processor currently rejects every route except Groq and calls only `transcribeWithGroq` (`apps/worker/src/media/transcription.ts:436-459,515`). `handler.ts` never attaches audio to provider input. The new package-native STT adapter therefore does not yet prove end-to-end native voice behavior. Wire the selected route into the existing processor or advertise only usable routes until integration lands. This is separate from text-response latency and must be rechecked against concurrent voice edits.

- Follow-up discovery 32 (OpenCode docs, 2026-10-06): the supplied [Go guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go) recommends a distinctive User-Agent and a stable conversation session header for routing/prompt caching. The live adapter already sends both (`packages/agent/src/providers/opencode-go.ts:44-50`), with the chat UUID supplied as `sessionId` (`apps/worker/src/agent/handler.ts:644`). Missing headers are therefore **not** a finding. Preserve session identity across turns, tool rounds and delivery retries; do not introduce a new session service. The guide describes Go as intended for coding-agent traffic. Otis's conversational business-memory workload needs a provider-fit check before relying on that subscription for platform access; this is not evidence that current requests are throttled or prohibited.

- Follow-up discovery 35: the stable prompt precedes changing workspace context, but current time is inserted before notes and before conversation history (`prompt.ts:59-69`; `context.ts:412`; `handler.ts:453-455`). A stable session header is not proof of cache hits. Consider keeping unchanged instructions/tools and older history in a stable order, placing per-turn time/retrieval updates near the request's end where each provider permits it. Keep time/timezone available for deadline interpretation; do not remove required context or add an application response cache for business mutations. Treat caching improvement as unmeasured until reported `cacheReadTokens` increases on representative turns. The adapter already parses cached token usage (`opencode-go.ts:153-180`).

- Follow-up verification: `pnpm exec vitest run --project pure packages/agent/test/provider-opencode-go.test.ts` passed **33/33** tests (449 ms reported Vitest duration). These use mocked HTTP streams and verify headers, incremental text, faithful tool continuation and error handling; they do not establish live gateway latency, native media support, cache hit rate or subscription suitability. `git diff --check` passed with line-ending notices; audit-file checks found zero missing local links, trailing whitespace or conflict markers. This follow-up changed only the running audit file, with no provider requests using user credentials or application source edits.

- Expanded audit discovery 37: cron processes transcription, every recovery workspace's full model work, Telegram retries, memory refresh, all selected briefs and media cleanup sequentially in a single invocation (`apps/worker/src/index.ts:829-919`). A slow transcription/model round delays unrelated scheduled work. The brief sweep alone needs one discovery read plus three separate reads per ordinary enabled member before deciding it is not due: **17 members = at least 52 D1 calls**, already above the documented [Free limit of 50 queries per invocation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/platform/limits/), before the other cron duties. Split discovery from bounded job execution using the existing actor/queue ownership, apply due-only selection and explicit budgets, and avoid a single long model loop inside the global cron. Do not solve this merely by firing all work concurrently; the invocation budget remains shared. Source/call-count evidence is high confidence; actual deployed plan/load are unverified.

- Expanded audit discovery 40: the shared API helper clears its 30-second timeout immediately after response headers, before `response.text()`/JSON parsing (`api/client.ts:79-99`). A response body that stalls can keep an operation pending indefinitely. Keep the deadline active through full body consumption, remove linked abort listeners in the same final cleanup, and expose cancellation for read endpoints. React Query's `queryFn`s do not pass the supplied signal to the API (`api/queries.ts:69-119`), so cancelling/removing queries or changing chats currently does not cancel their network reads. Wire signals for disposable reads; a client abort must never imply that a business write was rolled back. Add stalled-body and navigation-cancellation tests.

- Expanded audit discovery 41: brief candidate retrieval takes the first 500 open tasks and first 500 warm/hot entities **ordered by ID before due/staleness ranking** (`brief/read.ts:236-247,277-286`). A due task beyond the 500 UUID-sorted candidates can be omitted while earlier future tasks consume the read budget. Select a bounded relevant candidate set using due/snooze predicates and deterministic priority order, or paginate before applying the existing selector; keep timezone/date semantics and dispute filtering in code where required. Last-contact lookup also recomputes active contact history through windowed event queries for every selected lead chunk (`brief/read.ts:195-221`); measure this before introducing an incremental projection. A new contact projection is optional and must replay correctly through Undo. Do not widen limits indefinitely or add a model to rank briefs.

- Expanded audit discovery 42: recording finalization reads each stored chunk in a separate awaited IndexedDB operation; deletion does the same (`api/voiceSessions.ts:314-339,380-389`). At the existing one-second chunk cadence, a three-minute note can require about 180 serial reads before review/send and about 180 serial deletes after handoff. Use ordered `getMany`/`delMany` in bounded batches from the existing IndexedDB library, await pending chunk writes first, and preserve missing-chunk checks, owner generations and in-memory fallback. No new storage layer or larger recording cap is needed. Actual device timing is unmeasured.

- Expanded scope check: export/backup commands are currently gated replies rather than an implemented export pipeline (`routes/commands.ts:521-532`). There is no live export path to benchmark or refactor in this tree. CSS uses bounded transform/color transitions and already respects reduced motion; no measured basis for a visual redesign or blanket animation removal was found.

- Expanded audit correction/verification: concurrent source edits have moved `resolveModelAlias` to module scope, so the earlier command-route parse blocker is no longer present. A targeted real-local Worker/D1 + web run now collected all six selected files: **62 passed, 1 failed**. The native voice test calls the turn handler on a `queued` run, which is refused by the active-run guard; this does not by itself establish a production native-voice failure. Native-audio attachment code now exists in `agent/handler.ts`, so Discovery 30/F13's earlier integration-gap statement must be reassessed against this changing tree. Do not remove the active-run guard to make that fixture pass. Exact command: `pnpm exec vitest run --project worker apps/worker/test/d1-economics.integration.test.ts apps/worker/test/brief.integration.test.ts apps/worker/test/voice-media.integration.test.ts --project web apps/web/test/shell.test.tsx apps/web/test/voice-upload.test.ts apps/web/test/voice-sessions.test.ts`.

- Expanded audit discovery 49 (small product improvement): the disabled brief panel says to configure a schedule but presents only a timezone editor (`SettingsPane.tsx:210-263`); conversational scheduling **is** supported by the existing `update_preference` tool (`tools.ts:1456-1468`). Add a concise conversational example or a prefilled composer action; optional time/days/enable controls can reuse the existing settings API if needed. Keep ordinary work conversational and briefs opt-in. Display missing schedule fields honestly instead of the hardcoded `08:30`/Weekdays fallbacks. This is discoverability/clarity, not proof the backend cannot enable briefs. Native browser fixture review at 390×844 and 1280×900 found the basic layout usable; mobile settings evidence: [screenshot](qa/efficiency-mobile-settings.png). This synthetic fixture does not establish live device/keyboard/network behavior or full visual approval.

- Expanded audit discovery 51 (real local D1): the application core took **7 D1 binding calls / 14 SQL statements to accept a message**. Dispatching a one-call fake-provider greeting took **45 binding calls / 57 statements**; capturing one new business through `upsert_entity` and a final reply took **90 binding calls / 112 statements over two provider rounds**. These exclude HTTP authentication, outer dispatcher discovery/handler construction, Queue and Telegram delivery. Profiles use the actual migrated D1 and live acceptance/dispatch/agent/ledger code; no remote model was called. The entity capture exceeds the documented Free 50-query invocation ceiling even if an entire D1 batch counts as one binding call. The greeting leaves very little headroom. Treat per-invocation database budgets as a first-order fix alongside latency: batch the already identified independent context/projection reads and publication bookkeeping, eliminate redundant round work, and checkpoint existing execution slices before exhausting a measured budget. Never rely on daily row quotas alone, or introduce a Queue hop for every trivial tool just to spread calls. Evidence: [local D1 profiles](qa/__snapshots__/efficiency-audit.worker.test.ts.snap). The local simulator permitted these counts; this is not proof a deployed Free invocation permits them.

- Observation 59 (live Go capability): both Muse Contributor models actually support nested `reasoning.effort` on Go Responses. Minimal/high completed and were echoed; invalid was rejected. Otis blocks all explicit Responses efforts locally. DeepSeek accepted low/high/max but Otis exposes no descriptor and rejects max. MiMo metadata advertises no variants despite gateway enum acceptance, so published controls need qualification rather than an invented universal reasoning scale.

- Observation 60 (actual deployed UX): a harmless model-list question completed in 21.8 seconds from run acceptance, after a business-memory read, and returned an incomplete model list/unmapped effort union. Give the agent the existing server model catalog in bounded context to avoid that unnecessary round and incomplete answer. This one run is not a latency percentile or a matched comparison to a different direct prompt.

- Observation 61 (native stream path): OpenCode's current request/stream code uses model-specific options, sorted tools/stable session headers and incremental text events. Google documents streaming and implicit Interactions caching; explicit cache management is unsupported there. Adopt these small behaviors in the current actor/SSE architecture. No dependency-stack copy or new caching/orchestration service is required.

- Observation 62 (media route evidence): Gemini 3.5/3.1 and Go MiMo 2.5 accepted synthetic native WAV; Groq's real WAV transport also succeeded. These are format/transport probes, not Telegram OGG/Opus, mobile-device or speech-quality evidence. Keep exact unsupported/unverified formats on the working fallback until measured.

These consolidate the discovery log; they are recommendations, not implemented features. IDs are stable references, not a priority ranking. S = hours including focused verification; M = roughly a day; L = multiple days. Confidence concerns source behavior, not predicted production savings.

The expanded audit's highest-priority finding is **F14**, alongside the existing route/publication fixes F01–F07. Real local D1 dispatch used 45 binding calls for a greeting and 90 for one entity capture. Count binding calls, SQL statements, rows and CPU separately; batching alone does not eliminate SQL or scans. The [documented Free invocation limit](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/platform/limits/) must be verified in the deployed execution context as well as daily quotas. Actual remote latency/CPU and local-to-production counting differences remain unmeasured.

| F04 | Patch HTTP acceptance into the query cache; load old run details when expanded. Make recovery conditional on disconnection or an actual gap. | Avoids 4+N HTTP calls per send/resync and repeated 2.5-second run/transcript polling. | M / medium: retain offline recovery and stable UUID reconciliation. | High; reproduction 5: 54 API calls for a synthetic 50-run snapshot; `snapshot.ts:34`, `ConversationScreen.tsx:348,440`. |

| F07 | Join/reuse trusted metadata reads inside each execution boundary; claim/update with RETURNING; allocate a step index without loading prior results. Batch adjacent step bookkeeping. | Reduces pre-model and per-tool waterfalls, read payload and write amplification. | M / medium: checks at a durable commit must still abort on failure. | High: `providers/service.ts:153,234`, `actor/leases.ts:77`, `agent/handler.ts:866-925`. |

| F19 | Use existing IndexedDB getMany/delMany in ordered bounded batches after pending writes settle. | A three-minute fixture performs 181 reads including its owner record, then 180 serial chunk deletes. | S / low–medium: missing chunks, owner fences and fallback. | Measured operation counts; observation 42. Device timing unmeasured. |

| F22 | Store tool history once and compact provider continuation metadata; derive wire replay from canonical durable history. Accept/version older progress. | Avoids repeated Go history copies: eight-round fixture is 156 kB versus 35 kB in the compact comparison. | M / medium: restart/exact-argument/receipt compatibility. | Measured checkpoint shape; observation 50. No production size or new serialization implemented. |

| F27 | Add the trusted chat ID to steering-message/activity predicates and relevant guarded progress checks, using existing indexes. | Replaces workspace-wide message search, activity scan and temporary sort with chat/sequence and chat/activity index seeks. | S / low–medium: follow-up during active tools, late-steering and retry fixtures. | Actual remote before/after EXPLAIN; observation 57. No schema change required; production speedup unmeasured. |

The actor is the execution and live-publication owner; D1 remains durable business/conversation truth. Do not relocate all data or introduce a second authoritative state store to fix a transport mismatch. There must be only one intended writer/executor per workspace, with existing D1 atomic preconditions/receipts covering restart and duplicate delivery.

| Placement / D1 replicas | Regions can reduce network delay; read replicas do not accelerate primary writes. Wrangler confirms the D1 primary in WEUR/LHR with replication disabled; DO placement/account tier remain unverified. [Data location](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/configuration/data-location/). | Measure binding/actor network timing before changing placement. Do not migrate databases or weaken read-after-write consistency speculatively. |

1. Add a small structured timing summary to existing logs: acceptance, dispatch start, context duration/query count, provider request, first text delta, final commit, and client send-to-first-paint/send-to-final. Extend the existing profile harness to count the outer authenticated/actor boundary and report binding calls, statements, rows and CPU separately. No heartbeat/table or prompt/body logging. Remote SQL-duration telemetry does not measure network wall time or Worker CPU.

2. Implement F01 + F03 with actor-owned liveness, and F14's invocation budget as one acceptance criterion. Prove real SSE receives text and completion without the 15-second heartbeat or 2.5-second UI fallback. Preserve stable IDs on retry, member/source scoping and pending clarification. Avoid moving a 90-call dispatch unchanged into another Free-limited invocation.

4. Repair F16 API/body deadlines and F18 finalized-voice retry independently; then F19 chunk transactions and F23 audio playback. Verify missing/lost responses, stable message identity, private access and range behavior. F17 session lifecycle, F24 settings reads and F25 Stop feedback are similarly small independent UX fixes.

Targets are engineering goals, not current measured promises: local feedback under 100 ms; first provider text delivered within roughly 50–100 ms of its arrival when live transport is healthy; one model call for an ordinary no-tool reply; no historical-run refetch on ordinary Send; no repeated database read loop to deliver tokens; SQL statement/row/CPU counts comfortably below actual Free limits. Model/network latency itself must be measured from the deployed region/provider combination.

Snapshots record 7 acceptance calls, 45 greeting-dispatch calls, 90 capture-dispatch calls and local query plans. Provider keys blank in the isolated config. |

| Final scoped link/whitespace/conflict-marker checks and `git diff --check` | Passed: eight audit/QA text files, no missing local links, trailing whitespace or conflict markers; screenshot exists. Git reports only an LF/CRLF conversion notice. Temporary browser viewport/tab and local preview server cleaned up. Concurrent source changes/commits preserved. |

The requested deliverable is an evidence-based inefficiency review and lean improvement recommendations. The following verifies that deliverable; it does not mark the proposed application optimizations as implemented.

| Trace the delay from Send to first answer and completion | Current acceptance/dispatch/provider/publication/SSE/client paths inspected; F01–F09 identify routing, serial work, delayed flush, completion and recovery costs. Reproductions prove timer/call-count behavior; deployed end-to-end time remains explicitly unmeasured. |

At `8c83f03`, current source still selects Queue first for interactive dispatch, publishes preview through three D1 calls and dispatches recovery outside the SSE actor; these remain recommendations rather than resolved issues. Both isolated suites were rerun against this current tree: **11/11 synthetic checks and 3/3 local D1 checks passed**, preserving the recorded 7 acceptance / 45 greeting / 90 entity-capture binding-call profiles. Primary focus: browser send → Worker acceptance → dispatch/actor → context/provider/tools → streaming and completion. Expanded focus: backend read/write economics, real local/remote query evidence, recovery/brief scheduling, voice storage/upload/playback, startup/PWA, API/session cancellation and lean settings/product opportunities.

This was a hotspot audit, not a complete security, dependency, visual/accessibility, date/DST, migration or device audit. An export pipeline is not implemented in this tree. The next eligible work is implementation of the conversational route and invocation-budget optimizations with real DO/D1/stream evidence; no release/design gate is marked complete.

headings: # Otis Telegram and model integration audit — 2026-10-06
## Native responsiveness: the lean implementation plan

claims.text: Status: audit and bounded live research complete; implementation/deployment and the explicitly unverified cases remain next steps. Scope comes from the user's attached goal objective and native-harness steering: reproduce Telegram voice/text failures, assess native interaction feedback, test model/tool/continuation integration and verify exposed thinking controls. This continues the [latency audit](2026-10-06-latency-and-efficiency-audit.md), with findings recorded as discovered.

- Telegram API evidence: [sendChatAction](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendchataction) expires after at most five seconds; that lifetime is Telegram behavior rather than proof of a hardcoded fake timer. Genuine active-run feedback must be refreshed from the execution owner and stop on completion/clarification/failure. The current API also supports [sendMessageDraft](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendmessagedraft) for ephemeral private-chat streaming, followed by a real final sendMessage. Assess this small native feature before recommending edit-message loops or a new service; do not publish invented thoughts.

- Discovery T03 (source/browser): the only typing call is in inbound acceptance (`routes/inbound.ts:88-100`); no executor refresh exists. The `5000` in the helper is a request timeout, not the status lifetime. Sends are plain final messages, with no draft streaming or reply-to-original linkage. Coalesce provider text into Telegram's existing private draft API and refresh typing only while genuine work is active; final delivery must retain its durable outbox/receipts. Add safe formatting later rather than dropping Markdown into a plain-text channel or creating a notification service.

- Concurrent correction: while inspection continued, external edits wrapped Groq's fetch and expanded quote payload aliases; `git blame` identifies the quote change as uncommitted. T01/T02 remain verified explanations for the reported deployed runs, but must not be reported as still unfixed in the latest local code. Verify the current patches and deployment state independently. Current live UI has Muse 1.3 selected and exposes no thinking choices for it, consistent with the registry's blanket Responses restriction; actual endpoint capability remains to be probed.

- Discovery T06 (current source): schema errors other than the special missing-deadline case still abort `collectAndValidateProviderStream` before returning tool feedback. The temporary recovery edit seen earlier was removed externally. Accepting the quote `description` alias repairs the supplied case, but other correctable argument errors can still turn saved work into generic partial failure. Keep authority/schema checks in the executor and return typed validation feedback through the existing tool-result loop; preserve action IDs and committed receipts during repair.

- Thinking qualification: [MiMo 2.5's current Go metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/models.dev/dev/providers/opencode-go/models/mimo-v2.5.toml) also has `reasoning_options = []`. The T10 raw endpoint accepts low/xhigh and validates the enum, but this does not prove the model changes its reasoning budget; a gateway can validate a universal field without applying it to that model. Treat current MiMo adjustable-effort claims as unverified until an upstream contract or controlled effect evidence resolves this conflict. Muse has stronger live evidence: selected effort is echoed as well as documented by the model provider.

Otis can use the same API-level streaming behavior as a native harness while retaining its business-memory guarantees. It cannot promise identical Gemini consumer-app serving capacity, model routing or latency. Our basic direct Gemini 3.5 text probe produced first text at 4.6 seconds; the deployed model-list question took 21.8 seconds from acceptance to completion with a business-read/tool round. These are different prompts, so subtracting them would **not** measure Otis overhead. A matched baseline is required.
| Priority | Concrete change | Existing code to use | Acceptance evidence |

| 1 | Return correctable tool-argument errors as rejected tool results in the same run; retain strict executor authority and validation. Show committed changes on genuine partial failure. | `run.ts`, `agent/repository.ts`, handler progress/receipts, `actor/dispatch.ts`. | Invalid quote/field argument after a committed write can be corrected without replaying that write; unknown/forbidden authority remains rejected; clarification/date rules still hold. Telegram shows actual saved receipts and the missing operation, not only “saved your message”. |

| 3 | Keep known server-confirmed model/catalog data usable while refreshing it. Smooth live rendering and avoid whole-history refetch per frame. | Existing Query cache, `useModels`, acceptance response/cache patching, memoized transcript rows. | New-chat input is responsive with already-confirmed workspace defaults; no cross-workspace credential assumption; changed controls invalidate their affected queries; stable old message rows do not reparse Markdown on every new delta. |

Use **Worker → existing workspace actor → provider stream → existing SSE/client**, with D1 at acceptance, business commands/checkpoints and completion, and Queue/cron for recovery/deferred work. Workflows may simplify a long background job if they replace code; they do not make this token path intrinsically faster. Continuous voice/realtime sockets, an SDK migration, a vector service or another orchestrator are unnecessary for recorded voice plus text replies.

| MiMo 2.5 | Success | Production-shaped continuation succeeded; broader smoke harness repeated a call | Go accepts low/xhigh and rejects invalid enum; native Go metadata advertises no variants. Honoring adjustable budget remains unresolved. | Go native WAV tone accepted; Telegram Opus/WebM/MP4 unverified. |

| MiMo 2.6 Pro | HTTP 200 then 30 s timeout | 45 s timeout before a call | Low/high requests timed out, then endpoint-unavailable 429; current Go metadata advertises no variants. | Groq fallback runtime receiver fix verified; native audio unverified. |

| Muse Spark 1.2 Contributor | Success | Success | Minimal/high complete and are echoed; invalid rejected. Official/provider metadata lists minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh. Otis locally blocks them. | Groq fallback path; native formats unverified. |
| Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor | Success | Success | Same live effort verification; Otis locally blocks them. | Groq fallback path; native formats unverified. |

| DeepSeek 4.1 Flash | Success | Success | Low/high/max accepted; metadata corroborates them; invalid rejected with generic 422. Otis lacks descriptor and rejects max. | Groq fallback path; native formats unverified. |

Unresolved runtime evidence: the historical Gemini model-list HTTP 400's precise cause is absent from stored diagnostics and was not reproduced by the current bounded cases; native desktop Telegram is not an enabled computer surface; actual Telegram OGG/Opus and Android/iPhone speech accuracy were not tested; MiMo effort semantics and MiMo 2.6 endpoint recovery remain unverified; matched direct/app phase latency and production Worker CPU remain unmeasured. Preserve these limits rather than labeling them passing.
